title: kv-cache: adaptive memory rebalancer and eviction policy to reduce spillover and fragmentation
author: Ethan Zhang
description: Motivation: We continue to observe elevated host-spill rates on long-context workloads due to KV cache fragmentation and suboptimal eviction ordering. Spillover increases latency tail and telemetry shows compaction is often blocked by scheduling decisions during moderate load. This PR introduces an adaptive memory rebalancer and a fragmentation-aware eviction policy to reduce host spillover and improve steady-state GPU memory utilization. Summary of changes: 1) Rebalancer: a background, low-priority compaction/rebalance loop that opportunistically coalesces fragmented KV pages on GPU memory during periods of low scheduling pressure. The rebalancer exposes configurable thresholds (fragmentation_ratio, target_free_bytes, cooldown) and a prioritized work queue so scheduling can preempt compaction when latency SLO needs to be met. 2) Eviction policy: new eviction_score that combines recency (LRU), frequency (LFU decay), and a fragmentation penalty computed from page occupancy histograms; this biases eviction toward small fragmented entries and reduces scattered free space. 3) Paging/spillover improvements: heuristics to prefer sequential page spills and limit host-page count per allocation to reduce I/O amplification. 4) Scheduler integration: the runtime scheduler now signals expected load windows to the rebalancer (low/medium/high) so compaction only runs when it is safe. 5) Metrics and observability: added metrics: kv.rebalance_cycles, kv.fragmentation_ratio, kv.eviction_score_histogram, kv.spill_io_bytes and per-route spill breakdown. 6) Tests and bench: unit tests for scoring logic, integration test for rebalancer preemption, and new perf benchmark harness that simulates long-context chat sessions. Backwards-compatible: all thresholds default to conservative values; feature gated behind config kv.rebalancer.enabled=false by default. Test plan: - Unit tests: run locally and CI (new tests added). - Integration: internal perf canary on staging for 72h; we ran three runs with synthetic mixes (few-shot coder, multi-turn summarization) - Benchmarks: end-to-end memory-pressure test showed reduced host spill bytes and improved latency. Performance results: - Median p99 token latency: -10% across tests in staging when rebalance enabled. - Host spill bytes: -38% on long-context runs. - GPU memory fragmentation ratio: reduced from ~0.42 to ~0.18 on synthetic workload. Risk & rollback: rebalancer runs at low priority and can be disabled at runtime. If any regressions observed we can toggle kv.rebalancer.enabled=false or increase cooldown. Related PRs: references earlier spillover/defrag PRs and aligns with ENG-4721 workload. Notes: This PR touches low-level runtime paths; reviewers should pay attention to concurrency in rebalancer and eviction scoring math.
